Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Coleshill Church of England Infant School.
'Let your light shine!'
On behalf of all of our staff and governors I would like to welcome you and your children to Coleshill Infant School. Coleshill Infant School is a caring, happy, nurturing and friendly school, with high expectations, a vibrant, rich curriculum and a strong Christian ethos. Every child is nurtured and loved and given the very best possible start in their educational career.
Our Christian values of Love, Honesty, Stewardship, Respect, Perseverance and Resilience and our vision ‘Let your light shine’ underpin everything that we do. We want children to develop a joy and love of learning in our happy, supportive and warm school community. We nurture and support every child to enable them to find and celebrate the light within themselves and each other and to achieve their highest potential.
We aim to provide each child with a secure foundation so that they leave Coleshill Infant School prepared for the next step in their journey with a love for learning, an excellent all rounded education and a compassion for others.
Our school offers a well-resourced environment in a beautiful setting with plenty of outdoor space in the Chilterns. Children are taught in individual classes where a passion for learning is at the heart of everything we do. We work hard to know our children, and nurture them as they grow into independent learners, providing them with opportunities to experience exciting lessons in the classroom, our onsite Forest School, as well as carefully planned visits and workshops to bring greater depth to their learning.
Our school website aims to give you a taster of the school, covering all aspects of school life and I hope you find it useful and informative. Naturally it can only give you a flavour of our school and we would welcome the opportunity to show you round. Should you have any further questions or wish to come and visit us, please do not hesitate to contact the school office directly at office@coleshillceinfant.school and we will be very happy to help.
Thank you for visiting!

Thursday 15th October at 9.30am
Tuesday 24th November at 9.30am
(please pre book your place by contacting the school office)
office@coleshillceinfant.school
Is your child due to start school next September?
We would like to invite you for a tour around our Outstanding SIAMS infant school (ages 4-7) in the beautiful village of Coleshill, just 3 miles from Amersham. We are a small, well-established, high-achieving and nurturing school which provides an ideal environment for your child to grow and thrive and prepare for their move to junior school.
Our current admission number is 20, which allows for an excellent staff to pupil ratio in a small, nurturing environment (max 60 pupils in school). We have welcomed many generations of local families, have a team of dedicated, long-standing staff members and have maintained our goal to help every pupil "let your light shine".
If you have any questions, please contact the office on 01494 727 206 or email office@coleshillceinfant.school
If you are considering us for a current school place, we have limited spaces so please contact us for a tour.

Governors
Coleshill School is part of ‘Chiltern Village Schools Federation.’ This is a group of small village schools who work together to ensure children are given excellent opportunities to develop morally, spiritually and academically, as well as develop their self-confidence and independence.
The Governing Board of ‘Chiltern Village Schools Federation’ have a strategic role in school development. Working in partnership with the Headteachers and staff of the schools in the Federation to play a part in their success. The Governors are committed to working to ensure high standards of achievement, behaviour and excellence for all pupils in the full range of the opportunities provided. It is also the responsibility of the governors to monitor the effectiveness of our Christian Vision and RE curriculum.

Maths
At Coleshill, our intention is to foster a love of maths that enables our children to become fluent, competent and confident mathematicians of the future. It is our aim to ensure our children develop a deep and lasting understanding of the mathematical concepts that we teach in practical and creative ways. We aim to provide experiences that help to develop a growth mindset, allowing us to embrace challenge, encourage perseverance and celebrate resilience when solving problems that require critical thinking and logical reasoning. We aim to form a solid foundation in the basic building blocks of maths by applying our skills in order to solve real life problems based in the real world while also discovering the wonder of maths, having opportunities to make links between learning and to see mathematical patterns.
In Reception, Maths writing is taught within our Early Years Curriculum and at Key Stage 1, both Year 1 and Year 2 study different Maths units across the year. Please read our Maths Policy and Progression of Skills for further information:
Here is what some of our pupils say about why it is important to learn Maths and what they have enjoyed learning the most:
Dougie – I like the challenging Tiny Turtles questions
Joshua – I liked it when we did the measuring with the different measuring jugs and bottles
Luka – I liked measuring and pouring the different amounts of water into to the pots
Harry – I liked doing to the extra challenge in the early morning work
Oliver – I really liked it when we learned about time because I found it interesting and I always wanted to learn how to tell them time. Now I can!
James – I liked using the pizzas to learn about fractions!
Freddie – I like the maths puzzles because we did a huge one on the board, it was hard but it was really fun!
Jaxon – I liked using “jaxon fraction” to remember what fractions are!

Music
At Coleshill, our intention is to foster a love of maths that enables our children to become fluent, competent and confident mathematicians of the future. It is our aim to ensure our children develop a deep and lasting understanding of the mathematical concepts that we teach in practical and creative ways. We aim to provide experiences that help to develop a growth mindset, allowing us to embrace challenge, encourage perseverance and celebrate resilience when solving problems that require critical thinking and logical reasoning. We aim to form a solid foundation in the basic building blocks of maths by applying our skills in order to solve real life problems based in the real world while also discovering the wonder of maths, having opportunities to make links between learning and to see mathematical patterns.
In Reception, music is taught within our Early Years Curriculum and at Key Stage 1, both Year 1 and Year 2 follow the Charanga Scheme of Learning. This is complemented by learning drumming in Year 1 and the recorder in Year 2. Please read our Music Policy and Progression of Skills for further information
Here is what some of our pupils say about why it is important to learn Music and what they have enjoyed learning the most:
Luka – I liked it when we did the recorder concert, it was fun learning all of the songs and how to move our fingers on the recorder.
Quinn – I liked it when Mr Bass showed a video of him in his own band!
Oliver – I like it when we sing different songs.
Joshua – I like listening to the music, I liked the sound it made.

News & Events
Recent Trips, Workshops and Events
On Thursday 13th March, the whole school went on a fantastic school trip to the Roald Dahl Gallery in Aylesbury as part of our English and Science curriculum. The children did some brilliant workshops, a Roald Dahl science adventure and an enormous crocodile session. They had a wonderful time and learned a lot!
On Thursday 16th October, the whole school went on a visit to Windsor Castle, as part of our Humanities curriculum. The children took part in a workshops "All about castles" and were very well behaved exploring the grounds and castle.
On Monday 13th October we had a visit from Perform to do a drama workshop - the children really enjoyed themselves!
On Thursday 3rd April, the wonderful Kalpesh from KZ Dance visited us to do a Bollywood dance workshop and Holi celebrations with powder paint in the playground.
Trip to Chiltern Open Air Museum - Thursday 22nd January
Friday 13th December - Grandparents' morning - the children enjoyed a morning of crafting with their grandparents/relatives who were invited into school for the morning
On Wednesday 18th December 2024 we all enjoyed our Christmas Panto where they performed Jack and the Beanstalk...oh no they didn't...oh yes they did! The children were a great audience and we're sure it inspired many on their journey to become Proud Performers!
On 18th October 2024, Year 1 and Year 2 travelled to Holmer Green Senior School to participate in an inter-school football festival. The children all had a brilliant time in the sunshine and fresh air, using gross motor skills and coordination.
On 17th October 2024 the whole school went on a trip to The Lookout Centre in Bracknell as part of our science curriculum. The children took part in a nature workshop and explored the fascinating exhibits in the centre.
Wednesday 12th June 2024 Today, we finally got to hold our chicks! We were all very excited but made sure we were all very careful and gentle.
Monday 10th June 2024 As part of our Art unit on Sculpture, Year 2 had a visit from Mrs Keep who showed us all how to centre clay and throw a pot on her pottery wheel. We also talked about different ways we can decorate it and how it gets fired in the kiln. We looked at lots of things she has made and had a go using the wheel ourselves - it was much harder (and much more slippery!) than we thought it would be!
Wednesday 5th June 2024 On Monday, we were all very excited to have some eggs arrive at our school in an incubator. Today, they started to hatch!
Thursday 23rd May 2024 Year 2 were very excited today to release our three butterflies into the garden. The two remaining chrysalides will be going home with one of us to be looked after until they also emerge! We have very much enjoyed watching grow from tiny caterpillars.
Wednesday 22nd May 2024 - The Year 2 children did a fabulous job performing their recorder concert to parents and other family members. They played eight different songs in total and really enjoyed performing for everyone. Thank you to everyone who came!
On Friday 10th May 2024 Year 1 and 2 travelled to Holmer Green Senior school for an inter-school athletics festival. They took part in a number of sporting activities and had a brilliant afternoon.
On Friday 19th April 2024 our Reception class travelled to Holmer Green junior school for an inter-school multisports festival. They took part in a number of sporting activities, which worked on ther gross motor skills, balance and fitness
Year 2 had a visit from the NSPCC and talked about the importance of "Speak out, stay safe". We talked about safe adults we could speak to in and out of school, and thought about a safe space we could go to if we needed.
On Friday 19th January 2024 our Reception class travelled to Holmer Green junior school for an inter-school gymnastics festival. They took part in a number of gymnastics based activities, which worked on ther gross motor skills, balance and flexibility.
The children had a fantastic time at Whipsnade zoo on 28th November 2023, learning about animals and their habitats and behaviour. They explored the zoo and did educational workshops with the staff.
Om 29th September 2023, Year 1 and Year 2 travelled to Holmer Green Senior School to participate in an inter-school football festival. The children all had a brilliant time in the sunshine and fresh air, using gross motor skills and coordination.

At Coleshill, our intention is to stimulate and excite children’s curiosity, developing a sense of ‘awe and wonder’ about the world around them in line with our Christian Vision ‘Let your Light Shine’. We endeavour to provide all children with a purposeful, progressive, language rich science curriculum which is engaging for all. We aim to create learners who are equipped with the skills and knowledge to help them understand how science can affect our lives today and in the future. We provide an ambitious curriculum with high expectations and endeavour to develop children’s resilience and encourage a ‘have a go’ attitude during their scientific enquiries. We ensure that skills are built-on and developed throughout the children’s time at our school so that they can use equipment, conduct experiments, build arguments and explain concepts confidently.

SEND
COLESHILL CHURCH OF ENGLAND INFANT SCHOOL ‘Let your light shine’ SEND Vision
At Coleshill CE Infant School, we believe passionately in the importance of inclusion and equality for all children and adults and strive to ensure that these values are at the heart of our SEND practices. We will always involve parents and children in key decisions, as well as planning and reviewing progress; we know that parents are the first educators of their child and that we need their knowledge and co-operation to plan effectively. We know that the earlier we identify SEND and provide support, the more successful our children will be. We are committed to providing expert support and resources for children with SEND to fulfil their individual potential. Our staff work together with external agencies to effectively to meet every child's needs and ensure that no child falls through the net. Our starting point is to guarantee a whole -school approach to providing for the needs of children with SEND. Every child is getting their needs met through high quality first teaching. This is supported by enthusiastic, well trained teaching and support staff who understand how to implement effective strategies to ensure that all SEND pupils make the best progress possible. In other words, we make sure that all staff have the knowledge and skills to support all children, including those with SEND, throughout our School. Governors are fully involved in the process and attend meetings regularly, holding all stakeholders to account and rigorous tracking ensures that areas of need are identified quickly, and interventions are put in place to enable the gap to be closed.
